messages.content: Write a customer case study about a company that adopted a continuous delivery platform and now deploys more often. Around 250 words.

**Meridian Freight Systems: Thursday nights became Tuesday afternoons**

Meridian Freight makes routing software for regional trucking firms. Through 2023 it released once every three weeks on a Thursday night, four engineers on a conference bridge, working from a rollback plan nobody had ever practiced.

"Release night wasn't the part that worried me," says Dana Okonkwo, who heads platform engineering. "It was shipping six weeks of changes at once and having no idea which one broke production."

The company moved onto a continuous delivery platform in March 2024. The vendor estimated two weeks for the migration. It took eleven, and Meridian caused most of the gap: the test suite had been flaky for years, and nobody had noticed, because releases were rare enough to shepherd through by hand. Five of the eleven weeks went to repairing tests before a pipeline ran at all.

Twelve months on, the numbers: roughly 40 deploys a week, against 17 in all of 2023. Merge to production has a median of 22 minutes. Change failure rate sits at 3.1%, with no honest comparison point, because Meridian never measured it before.

Plenty stayed put. On-call is the same size. Support volume hasn't moved. Okonkwo says so without dressing it up: "We ship more often. No customer asked for that. What they got is a bug reported Monday morning fixed Monday afternoon, instead of waiting for the next window."

Meridian runs one Go monolith against one database. Anyone carrying more services, or a compliance sign-off between merge and release, will see a different curve.

---
